items.title: Contents remains an inline wrapping strip instead of scalable navigation
items.observation: Desktop and 375 by 812 operation again showed Contents as an inline module-button strip that displaces the lesson.
items.user_impact: The control works at the current size but is weaker than its label promises and degrades as modules grow.
evidence: Contents was operated at desktop and 375 by 812; the strip remained inline.
The earlier interaction walk measured a 71-node injection and nine chips wrapping to two rows.
items.cause: Module navigation is conditionally rendered inside the lesson composition.
items.recommendation: Use a semantic disclosure or drawer with a heading, current-module state, focus management, and independent mobile scrolling.
acceptance_checks: Contents exposes a named navigation region.
Open moves focus into navigation and close returns it.
Twenty modules remain usable at 320 pixels without unexpected lesson displacement.
items.disposition_reason: Reproduced in the current desktop and mobile walkthrough; severity reduced from high because the present module count remains usable.

items.title: Lesson state persists but is not addressable
items.observation: Moving between lessons left the URL unchanged while visible progress survived reload in the same browser.
items.user_impact: A learner cannot bookmark, copy, or share a particular lesson or resume it on another device from a link.
evidence: The URL remained unchanged from page 27 to 28.
Source inspection found internal page-index persistence but no hash, query, History API, or route update.
items.cause: Lesson identity exists only as internal state rather than an address contract.
items.recommendation: Give each lesson a stable slug or index in the URL and keep local progress as a fallback.
acceptance_checks: Navigating changes the address without full reload.
A copied URL opens the same lesson.
Back-forward traverses lesson history.
Local progress restores only when no explicit lesson address is supplied.
items.disposition_reason: Reproduced directly; the original critical rating was recalibrated to medium because core course completion remains possible.

items.title: Keyboard acceleration and visible focus need targeted verification
items.observation: ArrowRight did not advance, but native previous and next buttons remained keyboard reachable; the current run did not capture a complete focus-visibility sequence.
items.user_impact: Keyboard users can operate native controls, but course-level navigation speed and focus visibility are not fully proven.
evidence: ArrowRight produced no lesson change.
Tab operation reached native navigation controls.
The current run did not retain browser-backed focus screenshots for every control family.
items.cause: The earlier record bundled an optional shortcut with an unverified claim of keyboard lockout.
items.recommendation: Verify focus-visible treatment across control families; add optional shortcuts only when documented and non-conflicting.
acceptance_checks: All unique controls show visible focus at desktop and mobile widths.
Every representative task completes with native keyboard operation.
Any shortcut avoids active form controls and is documented.
items.disposition_reason: The identity remains relevant, but the earlier lockout wording was overbroad; native controls were reachable and focus visibility still needs direct evidence.

items.title: Dynamic lesson changes lack semantic regions and announcement
items.observation: The rendered document still had no header, nav, main, footer landmarks or live region while lesson content changed inside generic containers.
items.user_impact: Screen-reader users receive weaker orientation and no explicit notification when the active lesson changes.
evidence: Current DOM inspection found zero semantic landmarks and zero live regions.
items.cause: The single-page shell owns transitions without semantic page or announcement primitives.
items.recommendation: Add semantic shell regions, named course navigation, one main heading, and predictable focus placement or a polite lesson-status announcement.
acceptance_checks: The accessibility tree exposes intentional semantic regions.
Lesson changes announce the new module and title once.
Focus remains predictable after navigation.
items.disposition_reason: Reproduced through current DOM inspection; severity recalibrated from high to medium because native controls remain operable.

items.title: Declared font stack does not prove unavailable rendering
items.observation: Cambria, Georgia, Calibri, and Arial resolved in the tested browser; a platform-named declaration alone cannot establish user-visible failure.
items.user_impact: No current user impact was demonstrated in the tested environment.
evidence: Rendered font availability was checked in the connected browser and the declared families were available.
No cross-platform screenshot difference was produced.
items.cause: The original audit promoted a source heuristic without rendered or platform evidence.
items.recommendation: Preserve the current type intent; report a font issue only when representative rendering shows a material mismatch.
acceptance_checks: Any future font finding includes rendered comparison or confirmed fallback behavior on an affected platform.
items.disposition_reason: Cleared as a defect after rendered availability evidence contradicted the universal Windows-only claim.

items.title: Typography role proliferation needs task-based confirmation
items.observation: The earlier audit measured eight sizes on page one and demonstrated a reduced type scale, but the current run did not show that the existing scale causes a reading or hierarchy failure.
items.user_impact: Some states may feel mechanically over-styled, but a material learner-task cost is not yet established.
evidence: Baseline measured eight distinct sizes on page one.
Before and after evidence showed a coherent alternative, not proof that the original blocks a task.
items.cause: A style-count signal was treated as a verdict without a falsification task.
items.recommendation: Sample representative lesson, quiz, transcript, and summary states; simplify only roles that do not encode distinct meaning.
acceptance_checks: Each retained type role maps to a distinct semantic purpose.
A reading/hierarchy comparison supports any reduction.
items.disposition_reason: Preserved rather than dropped; downgraded to needs verification because count and taste alone do not prove user impact.

items.title: Short desktop lesson states may leave an unintentional dead viewport
items.observation: The baseline measured nine of twenty-one pages at 45 to 58 percent fill, while the current run verified mobile usability but did not repeat the full desktop fill study.
items.user_impact: Some short lessons may appear top-heavy on desktop; mobile task performance was not harmed in the sampled viewport.
evidence: Baseline per-page measurements covered twenty-one states and captured annotated before/after evidence.
Current 375 by 812 walkthrough showed usable reflow without obvious overflow.
items.cause: Composition does not adapt to short and long lesson-state density.
items.recommendation: Repeat desktop fill measurements and use state-aware vertical composition only where comparison testing improves perceived completeness.
acceptance_checks: All lesson templates are sampled at desktop and 375 pixels.
Short states feel intentional without harming long-state scrolling.
items.disposition_reason: The prior measurement remains material evidence, but the current run did not reproduce the full sample; retained as needs verification rather than silently omitted.

items.title: Missing search is not a current material defect
items.observation: A realistic Joker-rule lookup succeeded through Contents and module navigation in two navigation actions and about 7.5 seconds.
items.user_impact: The tested core lookup does not justify classifying absent search as a defect; unmatched terms may still benefit from an enhancement.
evidence: Contents to Module 3 to Joker rules completed directly in the current walkthrough.
The earlier fresh run also reported a three-operation direct hit.
items.cause: The baseline inferred abandonment from feature absence before measuring a representative lookup.
items.recommendation: Keep search as ENH-2 and require worse unmatched-term evidence before prioritizing it.
acceptance_checks: Search is promoted only when representative unmatched-term tasks exceed an agreed time or operation threshold.
items.disposition_reason: Cleared by direct task evidence; the related optional search opportunity remains under ENH-2.

items.title: All-caps kickers are a product-voice choice, not a defect
items.observation: The kickers participate in a coherent cream, green, and gold editorial course identity rather than a context-free template.
items.user_impact: No reading or task failure was demonstrated from the convention.
evidence: Current visual review found the overall system distinctive and subject-appropriate.
Hierarchy and primary actions remained clear in sampled states.
items.cause: A familiar style was treated as an AI tell without product-specific harm.
items.recommendation: Preserve the convention unless user testing shows hierarchy or readability damage.
acceptance_checks: Future changes preserve course identity and are justified by task or reading evidence.
items.disposition_reason: Cleared as a defect after contextual review; visual familiarity alone is not evidence of slop.

items.title: Speech availability and active-state feedback need environment-safe verification
items.observation: Clicking Play audio produced no visible label change in the tested browser, while source intends a stop state through speechSynthesis.
items.user_impact: A learner may not know whether audio started, failed, or is unavailable.
evidence: One live environment produced no visible state change and no console error.
Source and runtime observation did not fully agree.
items.cause: Platform speech capability and errors are not surfaced as explicit states.
items.recommendation: Feature-detect speech and expose idle, playing, stopped, unavailable, and failure states.
acceptance_checks: Supported environments display and announce playing and stopped states.
Unsupported or denied environments show a clear fallback.
Completion and cancellation restore the idle label.
items.disposition_reason: Reproduced as an evidence mismatch but retained at moderate confidence until tested in a confirmed Web Speech environment.

items.title: Three small-text color pairs fail 4.5 to 1 contrast
items.observation: Three computed normal-text pairs measure 3.44 to 3.45 to 1; the baseline title's fourth failure was an excluded alpha-compositing artifact.
items.user_impact: Small labels and controls are unnecessarily difficult to read for low-vision users and in glare.
evidence: Gold #C69B3F on green #13543E measured 3.45:1.
Green #13543E on gold #C69B3F measured 3.45:1.
Muted #8A7F6A on cream #F5EFE2 measured 3.44:1.
items.cause: Brand colors are reused bidirectionally and for muted normal text without accessible role variants.
items.recommendation: Split decorative gold from text-on-green gold, use dark ink on gold controls, and darken muted text while preserving the palette.
acceptance_checks: All normal text and control labels in tested states measure at least 4.5:1.
Hover, focus, disabled, and active states are remeasured.
items.disposition_reason: Carried after reconciling the count from four to three genuine failures; measured evidence remains valid.

items.title: One monolithic document is the shared change blocker
items.observation: The public 760-line, 86,582-character document still contains lesson content, navigation state, speech behavior, rendering, and styling with 256 inline style attributes.
items.user_impact: Addressable lessons, semantic structure, scalable contents, search, and consistent tokens all touch the same fused surface and carry shared regression risk.
evidence: Current source inspection confirmed 760 lines, 86,582 characters, and 256 inline style attributes.
items.cause: Content, view, state, platform capabilities, and styling have no explicit boundaries.
items.recommendation: Extract lesson data, route/state handling, semantic shell primitives, capability adapters, and visual roles; a framework rewrite is unnecessary.
acceptance_checks: Lesson content is data-addressable independently of rendering.
Route state is testable without the full page.
Storage and speech failures expose explicit fallback states.
All thirty-two lessons render unchanged before targeted improvements.
items.disposition_reason: Reconfirmed in the current source; severity recalibrated from high to medium because the present static course still functions.

items.title: One-page printable cheat card
items.observation: The sequential course still has no concise table-side rule reference.
items.user_impact: A beginner lacks a compact aid for the physical game where recall matters most.
evidence: The product frame still ends at a physical table.
Print CSS exists but the current run did not visually verify print output.
items.cause: The course optimizes learning sequence rather than table-side retrieval.
items.recommendation: Generate a one-page rule reference from extracted lesson data and verify print output.
acceptance_checks: One printed page covers the agreed high-value rules.
Print preview is legible without clipping at common paper sizes.
items.disposition_reason: Carried because the physical-table frame remains valid and no cheat-card surface was found.

items.title: Conditional rule search and jump to term
items.observation: Module-title lookup is fast, but terms such as courtesy pass, wall game, or Soap may not map cleanly to navigation labels.
items.user_impact: Search could improve table-side retrieval for unmatched terms, but current materiality is unproven.
evidence: Joker lookup completed in two navigation actions and about 7.5 seconds.
No unmatched-term benchmark was run.
items.cause: Content is navigable by curriculum structure but not indexed by term.
items.recommendation: Benchmark unmatched terms; implement search only if it materially beats module navigation.
acceptance_checks: A defined unmatched-term set is tested before and after.
Search results deep-link to the exact relevant lesson.
items.disposition_reason: Carried as an enhancement while the duplicate defect AS-08 was cleared by task evidence.

items.title: Per-module deep links are part of the addressability contract
items.observation: The user outcome is fully covered by AS-02's stable lesson and module routing contract.
items.user_impact: The sharing outcome remains represented without a duplicate implementation item.
evidence: AS-02 acceptance now requires copied URLs to reopen the exact lesson and browser history to work.
items.cause: The enhancement and the routing defect describe the same address contract at different granularity.
items.recommendation: Implement and verify through AS-02 while preserving this record and any decision attached to it.
acceptance_checks: AS-02 exposes stable module and lesson links.
items.disposition_reason: Merged into AS-02 without deleting the legacy identity or transferring a decision.

items.title: 375-pixel mobile pass completed
items.observation: The current run operated the course at 375 by 812 with usable content, fixed navigation, controls, and no obvious horizontal overflow.
items.user_impact: The most likely table-side viewport now has direct baseline coverage.
evidence: Rendered mobile walkthrough covered Contents, lesson navigation, reveal, transcript, and audio at 375 by 812.
items.cause: The original gap was missing test capability, not an observed product defect.
items.recommendation: Keep the viewport in automated regression coverage and verify any new templates.
acceptance_checks: The 375 by 812 representative-task suite remains green without horizontal overflow.
items.disposition_reason: Fixed as a coverage gap by a completed 375 by 812 live pass.

items.title: Surface resume and start-over choices
items.observation: Progress restores after reload, but the interface does not explain that a saved position was resumed or offer start over.
items.user_impact: A useful repeat-use feature remains invisible and slightly reduces learner agency.
evidence: The visible course remained on page 28 after reload from page 27 to 28.
No return-state banner or choice appeared.
items.cause: Persistence is silent implementation behavior rather than an explicit product state.
items.recommendation: When saved progress exists, show the saved lesson with resume and start-over actions.
acceptance_checks: Returning learners see the saved module and lesson.
Resume and start over both produce predictable focus and state.
items.disposition_reason: Carried after current behavioral persistence testing confirmed the hidden-resume condition.

items.title: Compact progress overview
items.observation: The interface shows linear progress but no compact overview of completed, current, and unread modules.
items.user_impact: Returning learners have limited orientation across the whole curriculum.
evidence: Current navigation and progress indicators were inspected across desktop and mobile states.
items.cause: Progress is optimized for the active lesson rather than course-level planning.
items.recommendation: Add a compact overview only if repeat-use testing shows learners need whole-course orientation.
acceptance_checks: Overview distinguishes completed, current, and unread modules without duplicating Contents.
It remains usable at 320 pixels.

items.title: Automated route, persistence, semantics, and contrast regression checks
items.observation: The course has no demonstrated automated coverage for the contracts most likely to regress during structural cleanup.
items.user_impact: Fixes to the monolith can re-break routing, resume, contrast, keyboard, or semantic behavior without detection.
evidence: Public source inspection found no linked regression harness for the audited page.
items.cause: The page evolved as a self-contained document without contract-level tests.
items.recommendation: Add a small framework-agnostic browser suite around routes, progress fallback, contents semantics, contrast tokens, and representative interactions.
acceptance_checks: The suite fails on broken deep links, persistence fallback, landmark removal, contrast regression, or unusable mobile contents.
All representative tasks run at desktop and 375 pixels.

items.title: Distinctive subject-specific editorial identity
items.observation: Cream, deep green, gold, Mahjong tile motifs, and editorial typography form a coherent course-specific system.
items.user_impact: The course feels intentional and memorable instead of like a generic dashboard template.
evidence: Rendered desktop and mobile states retained a consistent domain-specific visual language.
items.cause: The visual system is anchored in the subject and instructional context.
items.recommendation: Preserve the palette, editorial tone, and tile-specific cues through structural fixes.

items.title: Clear lesson hierarchy and sequential navigation
items.observation: The active module, lesson content, progress, and previous-next actions are immediately understandable.
items.user_impact: A beginner can start and continue the primary learning task without instruction.
evidence: Representative sequential navigation completed directly at desktop and mobile widths.
items.cause: The interface gives instructional content and one next action clear priority.
items.recommendation: Preserve this hierarchy while making lesson state addressable and Contents scalable.

items.title: Reveal, transcript, persistence, print CSS, and mobile reflow are real primitives
items.observation: Reveal and transcript controls worked, visible progress survived reload, print styles exist, and the sampled mobile viewport reflowed without obvious overflow.
items.user_impact: The course already supports meaningful learning and repeat-use behavior that should not be lost during refactoring.
evidence: Reveal-hide and transcript tasks passed.
Reload retained page 28.
Source contains print styling.
375 by 812 walkthrough passed.
items.cause: The application includes several product-specific interaction primitives despite its monolithic structure.
items.recommendation: Lock these behaviors into regression tests before structural changes.
